titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Félez Muñoz finds and rescues his cousins (tirada 131, lines 2763–2862b)
part: Tirada 131 · Félez Muñoz finds and rescues his cousins (lines 2763–2862b)

sentences.t: Alabandos ivan ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l: Praising-themselves were-going Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: So the Infantes of Carrión rode on their way, boasting.
sentences.n: Tirada 131 (assonance ó, ó-e) — Félez Muñoz suspects the Infantes; he turns back to look for the Çid's daughters, revives them and carries them on his horse to San Esteban de Gormaz; the news of the dishonour reaches the Çid; Minaya goes to San Esteban to fetch the ladies; Minaya's meeting with his cousins (Pidal: Félez Muñoz sospecha de los infantes. — Vuelve atrás en busca de las hijas del Cid. — Las reanima y las lleva en su caballo a San Esteban de Gormaz. — Llega al Cid la noticia de su deshonra. — Minaya va a San Esteban a recoger las dueñas. — Entrevista de Minaya con sus primas). The line-ends run Carrión, Muñoz, Campeador, coraçón …, with pu[o]den, Corpes, montes, varones, noches, coñosçedores: stressed ó, sometimes with an e after it. Pidal's note to v. 2763: 'Verso de encadenamiento, semejante al 2757' — 'a linking line, like 2757': the new tirada opens by echoing ívanse alabando at the end of the last. Alabandos = alabándose, the se cut to s (as ensayandos, v. 2746), 'boasting'; ivan + gerund, 'they went (on) boasting'. ifantes without the article, as often.

sentences.i: But I will tell you of Félez Muñoz, the nephew of the Çid Campeador: they had ordered him to ride on ahead, but it was not by his own will that he went.
sentences.n: The singer turns to his hearers (vos diré, 'I will tell you', future of dezir) and leaves the Infantes for Félez Muñoz, the nephew the Çid sent with his daughters (v. 2618). mandáronle = le mandaron, 'they ordered him': the Infantes had sent their whole company on ahead (vv. 2707–2711). de s[o] grado, 'of his own will' (so = su; grado, 'will'), and f[o] = fue, 'it was': in both words the o is Pidal's.

sentences.t:
En la carrera do iva doliól el coraçón,
de todos los otros aparte se salió,
en un monte espesso Félez Muñoz se metió,
sentences.i: On the road as he went, his heart misgave him: he slipped away from all the others, and Félez Muñoz hid himself in a thick wood,
sentences.n: carrera, 'road'; do = donde. doliól = le dolió, 'pained him', the le cut to l. Pidal's note to v. 2767: 'doliól el coraçón, le dió una corazonada, tuvo un presentimiento' — 'his heart gave him a foreboding, he had a presentiment'. aparte se salió, 'he went off apart'. monte espesso, 'a thick wood' (monte of wild wooded country, as the house montes, 'woods'). se metió, 'he went in, hid himself'.

sentences.t:
fasta que viesse venir sus primas amas a dos
o que an fecho ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
until that he-should-see come his cousins both two
or what have done Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: until he should see his two cousins come, or see what the Infantes of Carrión have done.
sentences.n: fasta que = hasta que, 'until' (f- for h-). viesse, imperfect subjunctive of ver, 'until he should see'. primas, 'cousins': the daughters of his uncle the Çid. amas a dos, 'both of the two'. o que an fecho, 'or what they have done' (que = qué; an fecho = han hecho), still hanging on viesse; the perfect sits loosely beside the past.

sentences.i: He saw them coming and heard what they said; they did not see him, nor knew the least thing of him — and you may be sure that had they seen him, he would not have escaped with his life.
sentences.n: Víolos = los vió, 'he saw them'. o[d]ió = oyó, 'he heard', the d Pidal's; una razón, 'a speech, some words' — the Infantes' boasting. nol = non + le, 'not him'. vi[di]en = veían, the old imperfect of ver, the di Pidal's (whether the i too is in italics was judged on the image and is not quite certain). dend, 'of it' (de + ende). ración, properly 'portion, share': ni dend sabien ración, 'nor did they know any part of it', i.e. nothing at all; Pidal gives no note, and the sense is taken from the context. sabed bien, the singer to his hearers again. vi[d]iessen = viessen, imperfect subjunctive of ver, the d Pidal's. escapara, the -ra form in its old pluperfect sense, here 'he would not have escaped'. mu[o]rt = muerte, the o Pidal's.

sentences.t:
Vansse los ifantes, aguijan a espolón.
Por el rastro tornós Félez Muñoz,
falló sus primas amorteçidas amas a dos.
sentences.l:
Go-off the Infantes, they-spur at spur.
By the track turned-himself Félez Muñoz,
he-found his cousins swooning both two.
sentences.i: The Infantes ride off, spurring hard. Félez Muñoz turned back along their track and found his two cousins lying senseless.
sentences.n: Vansse = se van, 'they go off'. aguijan a espolón, 'they spur hard' (as at v. 2693). rastro, 'track, trail'. tornós = se tornó, 'he turned back'. falló = halló, 'he found', with no personal a before sus primas. amorteçidas, 'deathly, in a swoon' (amorteçer, from muerte): left for dead (v. 2748).

sentences.t:
Llamando: “primas, primas!”, luego descavalgó,
arrendó el cavallo, a ellas adeliñó;
sentences.l:
Calling: “cousins, cousins!”, at-once he-dismounted,
he-tied the horse, to them he-made-straight;
sentences.i: Crying “Cousins, cousins!” he dismounted at once, tied up his horse and went straight to them:
sentences.n: luego, 'at once' (not 'later'). descavalgó, 'he dismounted'. Pidal's note to v. 2779: 'arrendó el caballo, "lo ató por la rienda"' — 'he tied it by the rein'. adeliñó, 'he made straight (for them)'.

sentences.t:
“Ya primas, las mis primas, don Elvira e doña Sol,
mal se ensayaron ifantes de Carrión!
A Dios plega que dent prendan ellos mal galardón!”
sentences.l:
“O cousins, the my cousins, don Elvira and doña Sol,
ill themselves exerted Infantes of Carrión!
To God may-it-please that for-it they-take they ill reward!”
sentences.i: “O cousins, my own cousins, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol, an evil feat the Infantes of Carrión have done! Please God they get an evil reward for it!”
sentences.n: Ya, 'O', calling to them. las mis primas, article + possessive. Pidal's note to v. 2781: 'mala proeza hicieron', v. 2388 — 'they did an evil feat': ensayarse, 'to exert oneself', as at v. 2388 and in ensayandos (v. 2746), here of their prowess on two defenceless women. plega, present subjunctive of plazer, 'may it please'. dent, 'for it, from it'. prendan, 'may they take, receive' (prender). galardón, 'reward', here bitterly meant.

sentences.i: He tries to bring them both round, but they are so far gone that they cannot say a word. The very strings of his heart were torn within him,
sentences.n: Valas = va + las: ir + gerund, 'he goes on turning them'. Pidal's note to v. 2783: 'valas tornando, "las va haciendo volver en su acuerdo"' — 'he is bringing them back to their senses'; a ellas amas a dos takes up the las. tanto son de traspuestas, 'so deep in a swoon are they' (traspuesto, 'senseless'); the de before the adjective after tanto is idiomatic and has no English counterpart. nada … non, double negative; pu[o]den = pueden, the o Pidal's, an ó-e line-end. Partiéronsele = se le partieron, 'they broke in him'. las telas … del coraçón, 'the membranes of the heart', what lies deepest (cf. v. 2577).

sentences.t:
llamando: “¡Primas, primas, don Elvira e doñ[a] Sol!
Despertedes, primas, por amor del Criador!
mientra es el día, ante que entre la noch,
los ganados fieros non nos coman en aqueste mont!”
sentences.l:
calling: “Cousins, cousins, don Elvira and doña Sol!
Wake-up, cousins, for love of-the Creator!
while it-is the day, before that enters the night,
the beasts wild not us may-eat in this wood!”
sentences.i: and he called: “Cousins, cousins, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol! Wake up, cousins, for the love of the Creator! Wake while it is still day, before the night comes on, lest the wild beasts devour us in this wood!”
sentences.n: llamando, 'calling', the gerund of v. 2778 again; the ¡ is Pidal's, and in doñ[a] the a is his. Despertedes = despertéis, present subjunctive as an urgent command, 'wake up'. mientra, 'while'. ante que, 'before'; entre, present subjunctive of entrar. ganados, properly 'livestock'; ganados fieros, 'wild beasts'. non nos coman, a subjunctive of fear, 'may they not eat us', 'lest they eat us'. aqueste = este. mont = monte, 'wood', the final vowel dropped, giving the ó. The print has no closing quotation mark here though the speech ends; one is supplied.

sentences.t:
Van recordando don Elvira e doña Sol,
abrieron los ojos e vieron a Félez Muñoz.
sentences.l:
They-go waking don Elvira and doña Sol,
they-opened the eyes and saw Félez Muñoz.
sentences.i: Doña Elvira and Doña Sol begin to come to; they opened their eyes and saw Félez Muñoz.
sentences.n: Van recordando, ir + gerund, 'they are slowly waking': recordar, 'to wake, come to oneself', not 'remember'. The present slips into the preterite (abrieron, vieron).

sentences.t:
“Esforçadvos, primas, por amor del Criador!
De que non me fallaren ifantes de Carrión,
a grant priessa seré buscado yo;
si Dios non nos vale, aquí morremos nos.”
sentences.l:
“Strengthen-yourselves, cousins, for love of-the Creator!
As-soon-as not me shall-find Infantes of Carrión,
at great haste I-shall-be sought I;
if God not us helps, here shall-die we.”
sentences.i: “Take heart, cousins, for the love of the Creator! As soon as the Infantes of Carrión miss me, I shall be hunted for in great haste; if God does not help us, we shall die here.”
sentences.n: Esforçadvos = esforçad + vos, imperative, 'take strength, take heart' (esforçarse; cf. esfuerçan, v. 2805). De que, 'as soon as, once'. fallaren, future subjunctive of fallar (= hallar): 'once they do not find me', i.e. miss me. a grant priessa, 'in great haste'. seré buscado, future passive. vale, 'helps' (valer, as in the house 'so may the Creator help you'). morremos = moriremos, the future with its vowel dropped. nos, the subject repeated at the line-end.

sentences.t:
Tan a grant duelo fablava doña Sol:
“sí vos lo meresca, mio primo, nuestro padre el Canpeador,
dandos del agua, sí vos vala el Criador.”
sentences.l:
So at great grief was-speaking doña Sol:
“so to-you it may-repay, my cousin, our father the Campeador,
give-us of-the water, so to-you may-help the Creator.”
sentences.i: In great grief Doña Sol spoke: “As our father the Campeador may repay you for it, my cousin, give us some water, so may the Creator help you.”
sentences.n: Tan a grant duelo, 'in such great grief'. fablava, imperfect among preterites. sí … meresca, 'so may (he) repay you for it': sí, 'so', in a wish, and merecer 'to earn back, repay', as at v. 2338; the line opens lower-case as printed. Canpeador, so spelt. dandos = dadnos, imperative + nos with the d and n changing places, as cortandos at v. 2728; del agua, 'some of the water', partitive. sí vos vala el Criador, 'so may the Creator help you'.

sentences.t:
Con un sombrero que tiene Félez Muñoz,
nuevo era e fresco, que de Valençial sacó,
cogió del agua en el[le] e a sus primas dió;
mucho son lazradas e amas las fartó.
sentences.l:
With a hat that has Félez Muñoz,
new it-was and fresh, which from Valençia-it he-brought,
he-took of-the water in it and to his cousins gave;
much they-are suffering and both them he-sated.
sentences.i: With a hat Félez Muñoz had — it was new and fresh, and he had brought it from Valencia — he scooped up some water and gave it to his cousins; they are sorely spent, and he gave them both their fill.
sentences.n: The tense runs from tiene, present, to sacó, cogió, preterites. Valençial = Valençia + l(e), the object pronoun 'it' (the hat) leaning on the word before: que de Valençial sacó = que le sacó de Valençia, 'which he had brought from Valencia'. cogió del agua, 'took up some of the water'. el[le] = él, 'it', the le Pidal's. lazradas, 'worn out with suffering' (lazrar, 'to suffer'). fartó = hartó, 'he sated them, gave them their fill' (f- for h-).

sentences.t:
Tanto las rogó fata que las assentó.
Valas conortando e metiendo coraçón
fata que esfuerçan, e amas las tomó
e privado en el cavallo las cavalgó;
sentences.l:
So-much them he-begged until that them he-sat-up.
He-goes-them comforting and putting heart
until that they-gain-strength, and both them he-took
and quickly on the horse them he-mounted;
sentences.i: He pleaded with them until he got them to sit up. He comforts them and puts heart into them until they rally; then he took them both up and quickly set them on his horse;
sentences.n: fata que = hasta que, 'until' (fata beside fasta, v. 2770). assentó, 'he sat them up'. Valas = va + las again. Pidal's note to v. 2804: 'Las va confortando e infundiendo ánimos' — 'he goes on comforting them and putting spirit into them'; conortar, 'to comfort'. esfuerçan, 'they gain strength, rally' (esforçar, here without se; cf. Esforçadvos, v. 2792). privado, adverb, 'quickly'. las cavalgó, transitive, 'he set them on horseback'.

sentences.t:
con el so manto a amas las cubrió,
el cavallo priso por la rienda e luego dent las parti[ó].
sentences.l:
with the his cloak both them he-covered,
the horse he-took by the rein and at-once from-there them he-took-away.
sentences.i: he covered them both with his cloak, took the horse by the rein, and led them away from that place at once.
sentences.n: el so manto, article + possessive; so = su. a amas las cubrió, the object said twice (a amas … las): their own mantles had been stripped from them (v. 2720). priso, strong preterite of prender, 'he took' (= prendió). luego, 'at once'. dent, 'from there' (de + ent). las parti[ó], 'he parted them (from there), took them away', the ó Pidal's.

sentences.t:
Todos tres señeros por los robredos de Corpes,
entre noch e día salieron de los montes;
a las aguas de Duero ellos arribados son,
a la torre de don Urraca elle las dexó.
sentences.l:
All three alone through the oak-woods of Corpes,
between night and day they-came-out of the woods;
to the waters of Duero they arrived are,
at the tower of don Urraca he them left.
sentences.i: The three of them alone, through the oak woods of Corpes, by night and by day, came out of the woods; they have reached the waters of the Duero, and at the tower of Doña Urraca he left them.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2809: 'señeros, "solos"' — 'alone'. Todos tres, 'all three'. robredos, plural here, 'oak-woods'. entre noch e día, literally 'between night and day': taken here as 'by night and by day', though 'in the half-light' (at dusk or dawn) is possible; Pidal gives no note, and the sense is not certain. montes, 'woods'. arribados son, 'they have arrived', ser with a verb of motion. de Duero, the river without the article. elle = él, 'he'. Pidal's note to v. 2812: 'Esta torre de doña Urraca estaría en el término que hoy se llama La Torre, siete kilómetros al Oeste de San Esteban de Gormaz, y no lejos de un pago denominado Llano de Urraca, a orillas del Duero' — 'this tower of Doña Urraca must have stood in the district now called La Torre, seven kilometres west of San Esteban de Gormaz, not far from a stretch of land called Llano de Urraca, on the banks of the Duero.' The text has don Urraca, as with don Elvira; Pidal's note says doña.

sentences.i: Félez Muñoz came to San Esteban and found Diego Téllez, Álvar Fáñez's man; when he heard of it, it grieved him to the heart;
sentences.n: Sant Estevan, San Esteban de Gormaz on the Duero (Pidal, notes to vv. 2697 and 2812). Dí[a]g Téllez, the a Pidal's: Diego Téllez (Díag = Diego, as don Dí[a]go at v. 2725). el que de Albar Fáñez f[o], 'he who was Álvar Fáñez's', his man; f[o] = fue, the o Pidal's. Pidal, in his note to v. 2822, calls him 'vasallo o pechero de Albar Fáñez' — Álvar Fáñez's vassal or tributary. elle = él, Diego Téllez. o[d]ió, 'he heard', the d Pidal's. pesól = le pesó, 'it grieved him'; de coraçón, 'from the heart'.

sentences.t:
priso bestias e vestidos de pro,
hiva reçebir a don Elvira e a doña Sol;
en Sant Estevan dentro las metió,
quanto él mejor puede allí las ondró.
sentences.l:
he-took mounts and garments of worth,
he-went to-receive don Elvira and doña Sol;
in Sant Estevan within them he-put,
as-much he best can there them he-honoured.
sentences.i: he took mounts and fine clothes and went to meet Doña Elvira and Doña Sol; he brought them into San Esteban and there did them all the honour he could.
sentences.n: priso, 'he took', as at v. 2808. bestias, 'mounts, beasts to ride'. de pro, 'of worth, fine'. hiva = iva, 'he went', the h only a spelling; ir + infinitive without a: hiva reçebir, 'went to receive'. dentro las metió, 'he brought them inside'. quanto él mejor puede, 'as best he can', present among preterites. ondró = honró, 'did honour to' (ondra, 'honour').

sentences.t:
Los de Sant Estevan, siempre mesurados son,
quando sabien esto, pesóles de coraçón;
a las fijas del Çid danles e[n]ffurçió[n].
Allí sovieron ellas fata que sanas son.
sentences.l:
Those of Sant Estevan, always courteous they-are,
when they-knew this, it-grieved-them from heart;
to the daughters of-the Çid they-give-them provision.
There stayed they until that well they-are.
sentences.i: The people of San Esteban — courteous men they have always been — were grieved to the heart when they learned of this, and they furnish the Çid's daughters with provision. There the ladies stayed until they were well.
sentences.n: Los de Sant Estevan, 'the men of San Esteban'; siempre mesurados son, a clause thrown in, 'they are always courteous' (mesurado, 'measured, courteous'). sabien, imperfect, 'they learned'. pesóles = les pesó. danles = les dan, 'they give them'. Pidal's note to v. 2822: 'enfurçión (igual en 2840) era el tributo de viandas, granos y vino que pagaba el pechero al señor por razón del solar que éste le daba. El que inicia la hospitalidad que los de San Esteban dan a las hijas del Cid es un Diego Téllez, vasallo o pechero de Albar Fáñez, v. 2814, y él y otros como él pagarían este tributo' — 'enfurçión was the tribute of food, grain and wine the tenant paid his lord for the holding the lord gave him. The one who begins the hospitality is a Diego Téllez, vassal or tributary of Álvar Fáñez, and he and others like him would pay this tribute.' His '2840' should be 2849, where the word comes again: a misprint in the note. e[n]ffurçió[n], both n's Pidal's. sovieron, strong preterite of seer, 'they stayed' (= estuvieron; cf. sovo, v. 907). sanas, 'sound, well'.

sentences.i: The Infantes of Carrión went on boasting. Through all those lands the news is known; it grieved the good King Alfonso to the heart.
sentences.n: Alabándos se[d]ían, 'they kept on boasting': alabándos = alabándose, as at v. 2763, and se[d]ían = seían, imperfect of seer ('to sit, be') with a gerund, 'to be (doing)'; the d is Pidal's (whether the í too is in italics was judged on the image and is not quite certain). The line takes up v. 2763. The middle line is wholly Pidal's: he prints it entirely in italics, an editorial line not in the manuscript as he reads it, and gives no note on it here; it has no number in his margin, and the letter in 2824b is ours. nuevas, 'news'; sabidas son, 'are known'. de cuer, 'from the heart, deeply'. peso, printed without an accent, is taken as the preterite pesó, 'it grieved' (as Pesó, v. 2835). don Alfons, King Alfonso, giving the ó.

sentences.i: The tidings go to Valencia the great; when they tell it to my Çid the Campeador, for a long while he thought and pondered; he raised his hand and took hold of his beard:
sentences.n: aquestos mandados, 'these tidings'. gelo = ge + lo, 'it to him'. Pidal's note to v. 2828: 'un gran rato', v. 1889 — una grand ora, 'for a long while', the house rendering. comidió, 'he pondered' (comedir). la su mano, article + possessive. a la barba se tomó, 'he took hold of his beard', the Çid's gesture of solemn resolve (as at vv. 1663, 2476).

sentences.t:
“Grado a Cristus, que del mundo es señor,
quando tal ondra me an dada ifantes de Carrión;
sentences.l:
“Thanks to Christ, who of-the world is lord,
since such honour to-me have given Infantes of Carrión;
sentences.i: “Thanks be to Christ, who is lord of the world, since such is the honour the Infantes of Carrión have done me!
sentences.n: Grado a Cristus, 'thanks be to Christ', with the Latin form Cristus, as at v. 2477. quando, 'since, now that'. tal ondra … an dada, bitter irony: the 'honour' is the outrage. dada agrees with ondra, the participle taking the gender of its object.

sentences.i: By this beard, which no one has ever plucked, the Infantes of Carrión shall not have joy of it; for I will marry my daughters well!”
sentences.n: par, 'by', in an oath. nadi … non, double negative; messó, preterite of messar, 'to pluck (hair)': to pull a man's beard was the gravest insult, and the Çid's has never suffered it. Pidal's note to v. 2833: 'no lograrán el fruto de la deshonra', esto es, 'no lograrán deshonrarme' — 'they shall not reap the fruit of the dishonour, that is, they shall not succeed in dishonouring me': la takes up the ondra of v. 2831. que, 'for'. casaré, future of casar, 'I shall marry (them off)'; a mis fijas … las, the object said twice.

sentences.t:
Pesó a mio Çid e a toda su cort,
e Albar Fáñez d' alma e de coraçón.
sentences.l:
It-grieved to my Çid and to all his court,
and Albar Fáñez from soul and from heart.
sentences.i: It grieved my Çid and all his court, and Álvar Fáñez with all his soul and heart.
sentences.n: Pesó a, 'it grieved'. cort = corte, 'court, household', giving the ó. 2835b is Pidal's own number. The second line has no verb of its own and joins Albar Fáñez loosely to the line before (without its a). d' alma e de coraçón, 'with soul and heart'.

sentences.i: Minaya rode out with Per Vermudoz and Martín Antolínez, the worthy man of Burgos, and with two hundred knights, those my Çid had named;
sentences.n: Cavalgó, 'rode out'. Vermu[doz], the doz Pidal's: Per Vermudoz. el Burgalés de pro, 'the worthy man of Burgos', Martín Antolínez's epithet. dozientos = doscientos. Pidal's note to v. 2838: 'quales, "los que"; comp. 2879' — 'those whom': quales mio Çid mandó, 'whom my Çid ordered (to go)'.

sentences.t:
dixoles fuertemientre que andidiessen de dia e de noch,
aduxiessen a ssus fijas a Valençia la mayor.
sentences.l:
he-told-them strongly that they-should-go by day and by night,
they-should-bring his daughters to Valençia the great.
sentences.i: He charged them strictly to travel by day and by night and bring his daughters to Valencia the great.
sentences.n: dixoles = les dixo, 'he told them' (strong preterite of dezir). Pidal's note to v. 2839: 'les dijo encarecidamente', 'les encargó mucho' — 'he told them earnestly, charged them strictly'. andidiessen, imperfect subjunctive of andar, from the strong preterite andido (= anduviesen). aduxiessen, imperfect subjunctive of aduzir, 'to bring' (strong preterite aduxo), with que unsaid. ssus, ss as printed; dia unaccented as printed. This line is 2840: Pidal's margin label 2840 stands one line low, against Non lo detardan, but his other labels and his notes to 2838, 2839 and 2843 fix the count used here.

sentences.t:
Non lo detardan el mandado de s[o] señor,
apriessa cavalgan, andan los dias e las noches;
vinieron a Gormaz, un castiello tan fu[o]rt,
í albergaron por verdad una noch.
sentences.l:
Not it they-delay the command of their lord,
in-haste they-ride, they-travel the days and the nights;
they-came to Gormaz, a castle so strong,
there they-lodged in truth one night.
sentences.i: They do not delay their lord's command: in haste they ride, travelling days and nights; they came to Gormaz, a castle mighty strong, and there, in truth, they lodged one night.
sentences.n: Non lo detardan el mandado, 'they do not delay it, the command': lo announces el mandado. s[o], 'their', the o Pidal's. apriessa, 'in haste'. noches, an ó-e line-end. Pidal's note to v. 2843: 'Gormaz, situado a orillas del Duero. Su gran castillo es de la época árabe y tuvo capital importancia en la reconquista del siglo X, sobre todo en tiempo de los condes Fernán González y Garci Fernández, su hijo' — 'Gormaz, on the banks of the Duero. Its great castle dates from the Arab period and was of capital importance in the tenth-century reconquest, above all in the time of the counts Fernán González and Garci Fernández, his son.' fu[o]rt = fuerte, the o Pidal's. í, 'there' (= allí). por verdad, 'truly', filling out the line.

sentences.t:
A Sant Estevan el mandado llegó
que vinie Minaya por sus primas amas a dos.
sentences.l:
To Sant Estevan the message arrived
that was-coming Minaya for his cousins both two.
sentences.i: The word came to San Esteban that Minaya was coming for his two cousins.
sentences.n: el mandado, here 'the message, word'. vinie = venía, imperfect. sus primas, 'his cousins': the poem, like Pidal's rubric, makes the daughters Minaya's cousins.

sentences.t:
Varones de Sant Estevan, a guisa de muy pro[e]s,
reçiben a Minaya e a todos s[o]s varones,
presentan a Minaya essa noch grant enffurçión;
non gelo quiso tomar, mas mucho gelo gradió:
sentences.l:
Men of Sant Estevan, in manner of very worthy-ones,
receive Minaya and all his men,
they-present to Minaya that night great provision;
not it-from-them he-would take, but much it-to-them he-thanked:
sentences.i: The men of San Esteban, like the very worthy men they are, receive Minaya and all his men, and that night they set before Minaya a great store of provision; he would not take it from them, but thanked them warmly for it:
sentences.n: a guisa de, 'in the manner of'. pro[e]s, plural of pro, 'worthy men', the e Pidal's, giving the ó-e. s[o]s = sus, the o Pidal's. enffurçión, the tenants' food-tribute of v. 2822 (Pidal's note there), here offered to Minaya. gelo, 'it (from) them' and 'it (to) them' (ge, ancestor of se). gradió, 'he thanked them for' (gradir).

sentences.t:
“Graçias, varones de Sant Estevan, que sodes coñosçedores,
por aquesta ondra que vos diestes a esto que nos cuntió;
sentences.l:
“Thanks, men of Sant Estevan, who are discerning,
for this honour that you-gave to this that to-us befell;
sentences.i: “My thanks, men of San Esteban, men of good understanding, for the honour you have shown in this that has befallen us;
sentences.n: sodes = sois. Pidal's note to v. 2851: 'coñosçedor, "entendido, prudente", 3137' — 'understanding, prudent'. diestes = disteis. a esto que nos cuntió, 'to this that befell us', the outrage at Corpes; cuntió, preterite of cuntir, 'to befall'.

sentences.i: My Çid the Campeador, there where he is, thanks you warmly for it, and so do I, who am here. May God in heaven give you a good reward for it!”
sentences.n: gradeçe, 'thanks'. do = donde. ffago = fago (hago), ff as printed. estó = estoy. Affé, 'behold', with a que-clause of wish: 'behold God of the heavens, that he may give you', i.e. 'may God of heaven give you'. de, printed without an accent, is dé, present subjunctive of dar. dent, 'for it'. galardón, 'reward', the word of Félez Muñoz's curse at v. 2782, now in a blessing.

sentences.t:
Todos gelo gradeçen e sos pagados son,
adeliñan a posar pora folgar essa noch.
sentences.l:
All it-to-him thank and his satisfied-ones they-are,
they-make-straight to lodge for to-rest that night.
sentences.i: They all thank him in turn and are well pleased with him, and they go off to their lodgings to rest that night.
sentences.n: gelo gradeçen, 'they thank him for it'. Pidal's note to v. 2856: 'sos pagados son, literalmente, "están satisfechos de él"; comp. 248' — 'literally, they are satisfied with him': sos, 'his', with pagados, 'pleased', used as a noun. adeliñan a posar, 'they head off to lodge'. pora = para. folgar = holgar, 'to rest'.

sentences.t:
Minaya va ve[e]r su[e]s primas do son,
en el[le] fincan los ojos don Elvira e doña Sol:
sentences.l:
Minaya goes to-see his cousins where they-are,
on him fix the eyes don Elvira and doña Sol:
sentences.i: Minaya goes to see his cousins where they are lodged; Doña Elvira and Doña Sol fix their eyes on him:
sentences.n: va ve[e]r, 'goes to see', ir + infinitive without a; ve[e]r, the old two-syllable form, the second e Pidal's. su[e]s = sus, the e Pidal's. do son, 'where they are'. el[le] = él, the le Pidal's. fincan los ojos, 'they fix their eyes' (fincar, 'to fix, plant').

sentences.t:
“Atanto vos lo gradimos commo si viéssemos al Criador;
e vos a él lo gradid, quando bivas somos nos.
sentences.l:
“So-much to-you it we-thank as if we-saw the Creator;
and you to him it thank, since alive are we.
sentences.i: “We thank you for it as much as if we were looking upon the Creator; and do you give thanks for it to Him, since we are alive.
sentences.n: Atanto, 'so much' (a + tanto). gradimos, present of gradir, 'we thank'. viéssemos, imperfect subjunctive of ver. a él, to the Creator. gradid, imperative 2nd pl., 'give thanks'. quando, 'since, now that'. bivas = vivas.

sentences.t:
En los días de vagar, [en Valençia la mayor],
toda nuestra rencura sabremos contar [nos].”
sentences.l:
In the days of leisure, [in Valençia the great],
all our grievance we-shall-know to-tell [we].”
sentences.i: In days of leisure, in Valencia the great, we shall be able to tell the whole of our grievance.”
sentences.n: días de vagar, 'days of leisure' (vagar, 'leisure'). [en Valençia la mayor], the whole half-line Pidal's restoration (in italics), giving the ó. rencura, 'grievance, complaint' (cf. rencor): the wrong they will lay before their father. sabremos contar, 'we shall be able to tell' (saber + infinitive, 'to know how, be able'). [nos], 'we', Pidal's, the subject repeated at the line-end, as at v. 2725. 2862b is Pidal's own number. The speech, the tirada and the part end here.
